elicitation_input.prompt:
Please comment briefly on the following solution.
Question: "Find the minimum value of
\[2 \log_{10} x - \log_x \frac{1}{100}\]for $x > 1.$"
Solution: "We can write
\begin{align*}
2 \log_{10} x - \log_x \frac{1}{100} &= 2 \log_{10} x + \log_x 100 \\
&= 2 \log_{10} x + \log_x 10^2 \\
&= 2 \log_{10} x + 2 \log_x 10 \\
&= 2 (\log_{10} x + \log_x 10) \\
&= 2 \left( \log_{10} x + \frac{1}{\log_{10} x} \right).
\end{align*}By AM-GM,
\[\log_{10} x + \frac{1}{\log_{10} x} \ge 2,\]so $2 \left( \log_{10} x + \frac{1}{\log_{10} x} \right) \ge 4.$

Equality occurs when $x = 10,$ so the minimum value is $\boxed{4}.$"

llm_generation.text: The solution is correct and concise. The logarithm manipulations are valid for \(x>1\), and setting \(t=\log_{10}x>0\) implicitly justifies using AM-GM on \(t+\frac1t\). Equality in AM-GM occurs at \(\log_{10}x=1\), i.e. \(x=10\), which satisfies the domain restriction. Thus the minimum value is indeed \(\boxed{4}\).
